title: Adaptive staged promotion with safety thresholds for private control plane upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: implement an adaptive staged promotion workflow for private (VPC) control plane upgrades that automatically adjusts promotion fractions and dwell times using live telemetry so we can reduce blast radius while cutting promotion cycles. This ticket covers the orchestration layer changes, Terraform IaC hooks for staged rollout metadata, health-probe thresholds, and a safety controller that can evict or pause promotions based on combined quality and latency signals.

Background: Existing staged upgrade flows rely on fixed wave sizes and static dwell periods. We've observed both unnecessary conservatism (long dwell times when signals are stable) and unsafe promotion when a transient spike looks benign until it affects KV cache warmup. The proposed approach uses an adaptive promotion thermostat: it computes a promotion impulse based on multi-signal deltas (5xx rate, p95 latency delta, error-pattern regression, and synthetic token-quality evals) and maps that impulse to conservative or aggressive promotion actions.

Scope:
- Add IaC metadata fields in Terraform modules to annotate upgrades with policy (min_wave, max_wave, initial_fraction, adaptive=true, safety_thresholds reference).
- Implement an upgrade controller service change that consumes telemetry from the control plane and telemetry proxies and computes promotion actions (increase, hold, shrink, rollback).
- Define composite health probes that combine SLO delta, tail latency, and a lightweight quality-sampling job (sampled completions against a golden prompt set).
- Wire in automated canary eviction and rapid rollback paths (non-disruptive) for Private clusters.
- Provide console dashboard tiles and logs to make decisions auditable (links to snapshots stored in observability).

Non-goals: deep model QA or full evaluation infrastructure (we will reuse lightweight prompt checks and existing eval harness). Not handling multi-region cross-account promotions in this ticket (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules expose new upgrade_policy block with adaptive boolean and numeric thresholds
Upgrade controller honors policy fields and can compute variable dwell times and promotion fractions
Canary promotions automatically pause and shrink when composite health score crosses thresholds
Eviction path completes a safe rollback without tenant-level data loss and emits an incident note to the control-plane audit log
Integration tests in the staging environment validate a synthetic regression (injected 10% 5xx spike) causes immediate 2-wave rollback
tasks: Design policy schema and add to terraform/modules/controlplane/upgrade.tf
Extend control-plane CRD (metadata) to carry upgrade_policy reference
Implement adaptive promotion algorithm in upgrade-controller service (PID-like thermostat with signal smoothing)
Create composite health probe implementation and register synthetic prompt set job
Add unit and integration tests, including injected-failure scenarios in CI
Add console visualization: per-upgrade telemetry snapshot and decision timeline
Prepare runbook outlining manual override, emergency rollback steps, and SRE contacts
rollout_plan: Start with opt-in alpha clusters: create terraform plan that annotates an upgrade as adaptive=true and initial_fraction=2%. Run upgrades in alpha-tenants for 48h with full telemetry retention. If alpha is healthy, promote to beta (10% initial) with controller enabled. After two successful beta runs (no eviction and composite health score >= 90 for 4 hours), enable on a small cohort of production tenant slices (5%). Monitor for 72 hours before broader promotion. All promotions must have a manual 'hold' toggle and automated eviction criteria enabled by default.
rollback_criteria: composite_health_score drops below 70 for more than 5 minutes
p95 latency increases by > 45% relative to baseline for 3 consecutive collection windows
5xx rate increases > 2x above baseline and absolute > 0.5% for 2 minutes
golden prompt quality delta shows degradation >= 4% in sampled completions
